title: Character and personality
description: Say what a person is made of, and how they are doing.
grammar: ser and estar, and the words of character
grammarNote: Say what somebody is with ser: es generoso, es tímido. Say how they are doing with estar: está cansado, está orgulloso.

explanation.summary: Character is what somebody is made of, and Spanish splits it in two: ser says what a person is, estar says how a person is at this moment. Choosing the right one is the difference between describing a person and describing a moment.

sections.heading: What somebody is
sections.body: Ser with an adjective says what a person is, and it does not change: mi hermana es generosa, mi hermano es orgulloso, mis vecinos son amables. To say who somebody is, ser is the verb: ¿quién es él? — es mi primo. El carácter is the word for the whole of it, and la personalidad is the way a person usually behaves.

examples.es: Mi hermana es generosa y mi hermano es orgulloso.
examples.en: My sister is generous and my brother is proud.

examples.es: Mi padre tiene un carácter fuerte.
examples.en: My father has a strong character.

sections.heading: How somebody is doing
sections.body: Estar with an adjective says how a person is right now: el niño está cansado, mi madre está enferma, el jugador está nervioso. La actitud is how somebody behaves in front of you, and it can be good or bad: el jefe tiene una actitud muy seria. Some adjectives change their meaning with the two verbs: ser aburrido is to be boring, and estar aburrido is to be bored.

examples.es: El jugador está nervioso antes del partido.
examples.en: The player is nervous before the match.

examples.es: Mi madre está enferma y no ha venido.
examples.en: My mother is ill and she did not come.

sections.heading: The words you use
sections.body: Choose the adjective that fits: una persona valiente, tímida, generosa, amable, orgullosa, humilde, egoísta. The ending of the adjective changes with the noun: un chico valiente, una chica valiente. And when you describe a person to somebody else, describe what they do as well as what they are: mi vecino es amable y siempre ayuda a todo el mundo.

examples.es: Mi abuela es una persona humilde y nunca presume.
examples.en: My grandmother is a humble person and never shows off.

examples.es: Mi hermana es tímida, pero yo no.
examples.en: My sister is shy, but I am not.

items.note: Masculine: el carácter. How a person is made, with the good and the bad.
Feminine: la personalidad. The way a person usually is.
Feminine: la actitud. How somebody behaves towards you.
An adjective: un hombre valiente, una mujer valiente. The same form for both genders.
An adjective: un chico tímido, una chica tímida.
An adjective: un hombre generoso, una mujer generosa.
An adjective: un vecino amable, una vecina amable.
An adjective: un padre orgulloso, una madre orgullosa.
An adjective: un hombre humilde, una mujer humilde. The same form for both genders.
An adjective: un hombre egoísta, una mujer egoísta.

drills.prompt: Mi hermana es ___; siempre ayuda a todo el mundo.
drills.meaning: my sister is generous; she always helps everybody
drills.note: Ser with an adjective says what a person is.

drills.prompt: El niño es ___; no habla con nadie.
drills.meaning: the boy is shy; he does not talk to anybody
drills.note: Ser says what a person is.

drills.prompt: El jugador es ___; nunca se rinde.
drills.meaning: the player is brave; he never gives up
drills.note: Valiente is the same for men and women.

drills.prompt: El ___ de mi hermana es muy fuerte.
drills.meaning: my sister's character is very strong
drills.note: El carácter is how a person is made.

drills.prompt: Mi madre es ___; dice que sus hijos son los mejores.
drills.meaning: my mother is proud; she says her children are the best
drills.note: The adjective agrees with the noun: una madre orgullosa.
